questions.questionText:
Which factor of production is not represented in the list shown?
bananas a factory goats a risk taking investor

options.text: capital
enterprise
labour
land

questions.questionText: What do economies aim to achieve in tackling the economic problem of scarcity?

options.text: equal balance between public and private sectors
equal reward for equal effort
increased competition in the use of resources
optimum allocation of finite resources

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows a country’s production possibility curve (PPC).
capital goods
consumer goods
Which statement is correct?

options.text: A movement from X to Y shows a decrease in efficiency in the economy.
A movement from X to Z shows a discovery of new resources in the economy.
A movement from Y to Z shows resources are being diverted from capital goods to consumer goods.
A movement from Z to Y shows an increase in efficiency in the economy.

questions.questionText:
China, the world’s second largest economy, is becoming more like a market economy.
Which policy would contribute directly to such a change?

options.text: abolishing state control completely
encouraging consumers to spend more and save less
reducing exports and encouraging more imports
transferring wealth from the state sector to the private sector

questions.questionText:
Coal production in the UK has declined in recent years. One reason given for this is that the
social cost of coal production is too high.
What best describes the social cost of coal production?

options.text: all the benefits of coal production minus all the costs of coal production
the cost of the environmental damage caused by coal production
the cost to the government of subsidising the coal industry
the private costs of coal production plus the external costs of coal production

questions.questionText:
A central bank acts as a lender of last resort especially in times of financial crisis.
What is the purpose of this function?

options.text: to cover credit card debts of consumers
to provide liquidity to the banking system
to remove failing banks from the financial system
to safeguard the profits of the banking system

questions.questionText: What will cause the level of savings in an economy to rise?

options.text: a fall in investment
a fall in real wages
a rise in income taxes
a rise in interest rates

questions.questionText: What could affect the size of the labour force in an economy?

options.text: the existence of a trade union
the government’s immigration policy
the quality of university graduates
the ratio of male to female employees

questions.questionText:
Petrol (fuel) retailers in a country have noticed a sharp increase in sales in August when many
people take their holidays.
Why might this take place?

options.text: Consumers’ demand curve for petrol shifts to the left in August.
Consumers’ demand curve for petrol shifts to the right in August.
Oil refineries increase their output in August.
Travel companies increase their hotel prices in August.

questions.questionText: What is correct for firms in perfect competition?

options.text: They achieve economies of scale.
They are price takers.
They make use of non-price competition.
They produce differentiated products.

questions.questionText:
A film production company purchases a group of cinemas.
Of what is this an example?

options.text: backward vertical integration
conglomerate merger
forward vertical integration
horizontal integration

questions.questionText:
The table shows a firm’s average revenue and average cost at different levels of output.
When all output is sold, which level of output gives maximum profit?
output average average
(units) revenue (US$) cost (US$)
Which statement about total fixed cost is correct?

options.text: It falls as output increases.
It is calculated by adding total cost and total variable cost.
It is calculated by dividing total cost by output.
It must be paid even if output is zero.

questions.questionText:
A government aims to reduce unemployment through a supply-side policy measure.
Which measure would it use?

options.text: It would increase government spending.
It would increase tariffs on imported goods and services.
It would introduce retraining schemes.
It would reduce the rate of interest.

questions.questionText: When is a government said to balance its budget?

options.text: when all goods and services are taxed equally
when economic growth is the same in all regions of the economy
when its total income equals its total expenditure
when total exports equal total imports

questions.questionText:
In which case is success for the government in achieving the first aim likely to cause problems in
achieving the second?
first aim second aim

options.text: full employment price stability
high economic growth full employment
price stability stable balance of payments
stable balance of payments more even distribution of income

questions.questionText: Economic growth is usually measured by the annual change in

options.text: consumer spending.
gross domestic product.
the output of the manufacturing and construction industries.
the retail price index (RPI).

questions.questionText:
Four groups who are affected by changing economic conditions are creditors, debtors, exporters
and importers.
Which pair is most likely to be disadvantaged by a high rate of inflation?

options.text: creditors and exporters
creditors and importers
debtors and exporters
debtors and importers

questions.questionText:
A country experienced its usual August increase in the rate of unemployment. Unfortunately this
was followed by the loss of jobs resulting from the regular downturn in global economic activity.
Which types of unemployment occurred?
first type of second type of
unemployment unemployment
(August) (global downturn)

options.text: cyclical structural
frictional seasonal
seasonal cyclical
structural frictional

questions.questionText: What will lead to an ageing population if other factors remain unchanged?

options.text: a fall in the birth rate
a rise in the death rate
an increase in the age of retirement
an increase in the state pension

questions.questionText: Which change is most likely to be expected when an economy is developing?

options.text: birth rates increase rapidly
poverty rates fall
unemployment levels rise
the primary sector overtakes the secondary sector

questions.questionText:
Developing countries are sometimes given aid by charities and foreign governments.
Which aid programme would be least likely to lead to long-term economic growth?

options.text: the building of an irrigation system
the construction of a new airport
the distribution of gifts of food
the training of technical staff

questions.questionText:
It is estimated that in 2016 the Olympic Games in Rio, Brazil attracted over 600000 foreign
visitors.
What is likely to have been the result of this number of visitors?

options.text: a depreciation of Brazil’s currency
a fall in Brazil’s rate of inflation
an increase in the Brazilian government’s budget deficit
a reduction in Brazil’s deficit on the current account of its balance of payments

questions.questionText:
What is most likely to happen if South Korea builds a factory in Switzerland that becomes
profitable?

options.text: South Korea’s imports of goods will decrease.
South Korea’s investment income will increase.
Switzerland’s trade balance in goods will worsen.
Switzerland’s trade balance in services will improve.

questions.questionText:
A country has experienced a devaluation of its currency.
What are the likely results of the devaluation?
imports exports

options.text: price decreases value decreases
price decreases value increases
price increases quantity decreases
price increases quantity increases

The table shows the tariffs imposed on imported tropical fruit in the European Union (EU)
according to the degree of processing.
EU tariffs

fresh tropical fruit 8.0
canned tropical fruit 11.3
bottled tropical fruit drinks 23.6
What might be the reason for this pattern of tariffs?

options.text: to encourage imports of processed products into the EU
to encourage tropical countries’ exports
to help manufacturing industries in the EU
